newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian opposition chief rejects new parties.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian opposition chief rejects new parties.

text.p: The octogenarian leader of Nigeria's opposition National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) on Wednesday blasted the registration of five political parties by the military authorities, saying the exercise was not acceptable.

"Most of the associations with mass movement stature were scored poorly...yet the weaker ones received official nod," Michael Ajasin said in a statement faxed to Reuters from his home in Owo, southwestern Nigeria.

"Therefore, I reject and denounce the last party registration exercise and its outcome," said the 88-year-old Ajasin, who urged ..."Nigerians to remain calm and continue to pray to the Almighty God to soften the hearts of our rulers."

The electoral commission announced on Monday that out of 15 groups that sought to become political parties so as to contest elections expected to lead to full democracy in 1998, only five had succeeded based on stringent criteria like national spread.
All five are from the political centre ground and none opposes the military government.

Among those that failed to qualify was Peoples Progressive Party which paraded members of NADECO, a group formed in 1994 to push General Sani Abacha to hand over to Moshood Abiola, the detained businessman believed to have won an annulled 1993 vote.
